sources.citation: OLAC listing for onr (the Internet Archive 2023-11-30) and SIL.org archive listing for onr (the Internet Archive 2015-09-18)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Catalog pages only: SIL holdings for Northern One are literacy primers (Bifo Rit na Rait; Onnele Alphabet Wolwale/Rombar; Olaman!! 2017), a 2001 text collection (item 70110) and 2019 audio; the only descriptive items are the tentative grammar descriptions, which are not downloadable.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2013. 'One' language page, ANU Papuan linguistics site (the Internet Archive 2014-02-05).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Gives only the (Molmo) One segment inventory (10 consonants, 8 vowels); nothing on stress; refers to Molmo One, not Northern One.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark. 2006. Torricelli Languages. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language & Linguistics, 2nd ed. Oxford: Elsevier. doi:10.1016/B0-08-044854-2/04600-9 (author's PDF via the Internet Archive of ANU site)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only, p.1: 'There are typically no phonetically unusual segments in Torricelli languages, and, although stress is frequently contrastive, reports of tonal differences are rare.' No statement specific to One / Northern One.

sources.citation: Donohue, Mark & Melissa Crowther. 2005. Meeting in the middle: interaction in North-Central New Guinea. In A. Pawley, R. Attenborough, J. Golson & R. Hide (eds), Papuan pasts: cultural, linguistic and biological histories of Papuan-speaking peoples, 167-184. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. (scan, no text layer; scanned at 300 dpi)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. p.181: 'Tonal systems are consistently absent in the Torricelli languages (relevant here are the One varieties)'; p.182 Table 4 'Comparative suprasegmental inventories' lists One varieties Siama, Inebu, Romei with no pitch contrasts (Romei = the Romei-Barera dialect of Northern One). Segmental history of Romei (*t>r, *s loss) discussed pp.178-179; vowel/consonant inventories Tables 2-3.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 767-780. Pacific Linguistics C-38. doi:10.15144/PL-C38.767
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: One paragraph of phylum-level phonology (p.769: three places of articulation, no voicing contrast, 5-8 vowels, many fricatives) illustrated from Olo; nothing on stress; One appears only in the classification/population list.

sources.citation: Pehrson, Benjamin, Gibson Musi & Joel Malan. 2016. Tentative Grammar Description for the Onnele Wolwale [onr] Language spoken in Sandaun Province, Papua New Guinea. Ukarumpa: SIL Papua New Guinea. 62 pp.
